question.text: Ms. Ritu Kapoor, IC Chair at Godavari Cat III AIF, runs a MARKET-NEUTRAL long/short equity strategy using index options and delta-hedged pairs. The strategy is designed to be independent of broad market direction. Per Chapter 10, what is the MOST appropriate benchmark?

answer.text: NIFTY 50 TRI — since it is India's flagship broad-based index applicable to all Cat III AIFs regardless of strategy.

A FIXED pre-determined absolute-return hurdle (e.g., 10% p.a.) set by the Investment Manager at fund launch and disclosed in the PPM — absolute-return strategies are NOT benchmarked against broad-based relative indices.
S&P BSE Sensex price index — since the fund trades Indian equities, a price-only index is sufficient.
NIFTY IT Index — sectoral indices are the default benchmark for market-neutral strategies.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the benchmark for absolute-return strategies may be a fixed rate, pre-determined by the Investment Manager at the time of launching the fund scheme, such as 10 percent per annum. Absolute returns are not benchmarked against a broad-based market index or a relative benchmark. The Trap: Option A applies a relative benchmark to a strategy designed to be market-independent — any positive market year would show artificial "underperformance". Options C and D are sectoral/price misfits inconsistent with the workbook's absolute-return guidance. Note: The fixed absolute-return hurdle should be disclosed in the PPM at fund launch.
